chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Washa, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to apportion his moments between his companions, so he would look at one and look at another with fairness.

He said: And the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) never extended his legs among his companions at all, and if a man were to shake his hand, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not remove his hand from his hand until it was he who was the one to leave.
So when they discerned that, the man, whenever he shook his hand, would say with his hand, so he removed it from his hand.
ai.seo_question: What were the Prophet's (peace be upon him and his family) habits regarding fairness and handshakes with his companions?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) meticulous adherence to *adl* (justice) and *tawazu* (humility) in daily conduct, serving as a practical model for Shia etiquette (*adab*). The detail regarding the handshake illustrates his gentle leadership style, where he avoided imposing his status, thereby encouraging companions to mirror his modesty. This behavior reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the Prophet as the perfect exemplar (*uswa hasana*) whose physical actions embody spiritual virtues.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Jameel Bin Darraj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to apportion his<sup>saww</sup> moments (time) between his<sup>saww</sup> companions. So he<sup>saww</sup> would look at that one, and he<sup>saww</sup> would look at that one, with the fairness’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> did not extend his<sup>asws</sup> legs in between his<sup>saww</sup> companions at all, and if the man was to shake his<sup>saww</sup> hand, so Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would not leave his hand from his<sup>saww</sup> hand until it so happened that he was the leaver.
So when they (the people) discerned that, it was so that the man, whenever he shook his<sup>saww</sup> hand, said so with his hands, so he removed it (quickly) from his<sup>saww</sup> hand’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Washsha’ from Jamil ibn Darraj from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah would look to every one of his companions in equal proportions of time. He would look to this and then to that person.

The Messenger of Allah was never seen stretching his legs in a gathering of his companions. When he would shake hands, with a person, the Messenger of Allah would not pull back his hand before the other man.
When they noticed it thereafter a man shaking hands with him would pull his hand away quickly.”
